title: Ekalavya's Thumb
text:
Drona was the great teacher of archery to the princes of the Kuru royal house, and Arjuna was his favorite pupil. Drona had promised Arjuna that no archer in the world would ever be his equal.

One day a young man named Ekalavya, the son of a chief of the Nishadas, a forest tribe, came and asked to be Drona's student. Drona refused him because of his low birth. Ekalavya went back into the forest, made a clay image of Drona, and practiced in front of it every day as if before his teacher. He became an astonishing archer.

Later the princes went hunting, and their dog barked at Ekalavya. Before it could close its mouth, he shot seven arrows into it, filling its mouth without killing it. The princes were amazed and found him. Asked who his teacher was, he named Drona. Arjuna went to Drona and reminded him of his promise.

Drona went to the forest. Ekalavya welcomed him with deep respect. Drona then claimed the fee a pupil owes his teacher, and he asked for the young man's right thumb. Without hesitation Ekalavya cut it off and gave it to him. When he shot again, he was no longer as quick as before, and Arjuna was the greatest archer once more.
lesson: People with the power to open or close doors can use it to protect favorites at the cost of real talent. Watch whether your own rules and standards are serving the work or only those you prefer.
